claim.quote: Here we report a high-precision measurement of ... in units of the nuclear magneton μN with a fractional precision of 1.5 parts per billion (68% confidence level).

name: A parts-per-billion measurement of the antiproton magnetic moment

significance.quote: and is in agreement with CPT invariance
significance.value: Fractional precision 1.5 parts per billion; consistent with the proton magnetic moment and in agreement with CPT invariance

summary.plain: BASE measured the magnetic moment of the antiproton, how strongly it acts like a tiny magnet, to 1.5 parts per billion. The value agrees with the proton’s and with CPT invariance, and improves the previous best by a factor of about 350.
summary.technical: Two-particle spectroscopy in a cryogenic multi-Penning trap system: antiproton magnetic moment −2.7928473441(42) μN, consistent with the proton value 2.792847350(9) μN and with CPT invariance; improves the previous best measurement by a factor of approximately 350.

title: A parts-per-billion measurement of the antiproton magnetic moment
why_it_matters: The abstract says the result constrains the magnitude of certain CPT-violating effects to below 1.8 × 10−24 gigaelectronvolts.
